newsitem.title: FRANCE: France studying horses for Paris police.
newsitem.headline: France studying horses for Paris police.

text.p: France is considering deploying police on horseback on the streets of Paris, imitating foreign cities like New York or London, Interior Minister Jean-Louis Debre said on Wednesday.
"I'm not against it on principle," Debre told a news conference. "We're making a study at the moment which will take some time to see if police on horseback would fill a need."
Police in Paris currently walk or drive motorcycles, cars or vans.
"I'm opposed to nothing if it can lead to a fall in crime...and if that can reduce a feeling of insecurity," Debre said.
Those who favour mounted police for Paris say they could discourage crime by making the police more visible.
Laurent Dominati, a deputy of the centrist UDF which is the junior partner in the ruling coalition, floated the idea of putting horses into police service in Paris.
He urged the government on Tuesday to deploy existing mounted units of the Republican Guard -- the president's guards -- for police patrols.
The units, part of the paramilitary gendarmerie, are mostly used for ceremonial functions when, wearing resplendent Napoleonic-era uniforms, they escort the president's car.

The last time horses made a major appearance on the Paris security scene was on February 6, 1934, when the presidential guard charged a right-wing mob during disturbances aimed at overthrowing the government. Shooting broke out and several people and horses were killed.
A spokeswoman for the city hall in Orleans in central France, which has mounted police, said citizens overwhelmingly favoured the system. "It's been good for the city," she said.
